xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5071: overdeck.ai activate link: one Authorize click that names the bot and the machine

plan.title: overdeck.ai activate link: one Authorize click that names the bot and the machine
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The device-flow activate link a bot shows the operator (https://account.overdeck.ai/activate?user_code=...) opens a typed-code form: the operator clicks Continue, then Continue with GitHub, and the page names only the platform. PAN-5069 decision 3 requires one Authorize click on a page that names the bot and the machine. Part A (the connector) already sends client_name and target_name; the account service ignores them.
narratives.Proposal: Add migration 0003 with nullable client_name/target_name on device_grants; issueCode stores them cleaned by deviceName (controls and bidi removed, trimmed, cut to 64 code points, blank -> NULL). One confirmStep renderer names the bot and machine as claims with one Authorize button, used by POST /activate and by GET /activate when user_code resolves to a pending grant. A GET with a code that does not resolve renders the form with the error at 400 and counts against activate-fail (peek before lookup, hit on a miss). GET never writes device_grants. A Miniflare test proves the migration and link on real workerd. docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md documents the fields, the GET confirm step, the GET rate-limit counting and the migrate-before-deploy order.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Deploying the Worker, applying migrations remotely, or running wrangler deploy (operator-only)
- Any change to POST /activate/confirm, its same-origin Origin check, startGitHubLeg or the GitHub leg
- Showing client_name/target_name on the Device connected page, in devices.label, in the token response or in GET /v1/devices
- Adding a route-level rate-limit bucket to GET /activate (routes.ts does not change)
- Verifying the names against the directory or the machine; they are claims by design
- Changing src/lib/account/client.ts or pan mcp connector connect (Part A shipped)
- Defending the per-IP activate-fail window against cross-site GETs that fill it (accepted risk in the PRD)
- Any GET /activate request mutating device_grants (status, user_id or last_polled_at)

autoDecisions.summary: A GET whose user_code does not resolve renders the typed form with INVALID_CODE_MESSAGE at status 400, prefilled with the formatted code
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches POST /activate; a silent prefilled form would make the human resubmit and burn a second activate-fail hit.

autoDecisions.summary: GET gates only non-empty codes: peek activate-fail before the lookup, hit on a miss; no route-level bucket is added
autoDecisions.rationale: Mirrors POST /activate order; activate-fail already caps guessing, and a route bucket would also cap valid reloads without adding safety.

autoDecisions.summary: GET and POST /activate share one confirmStep renderer whose button reads Authorize
autoDecisions.rationale: Otherwise the typed-code path keeps "Continue with GitHub" and two confirm pages diverge.

autoDecisions.summary: Over-long names are cut to 64 code points (never a 400); control and bidi characters are stripped; blank stores NULL
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says trimmed, at most 64 characters; the client already cuts at 64; stripping bidi/control characters prevents visual spoofing on a page a human approves from.

autoDecisions.summary: When client_name is absent the device type (defaultLabel) stands in; the no-name sentence stays exactly as today
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps old clients and pan account login unchanged and avoids "unknown" on the page.

autoDecisions.summary: Names stay off devices.label and every API response
autoDecisions.rationale: D-17 keeps device labels free of hostnames; the names are unverified claims meant only for the approval page.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs state the deploy order: apply 0003 before deploying the new Worker
autoDecisions.rationale: The new INSERT names the new columns, so the new Worker on the old schema 500s every device-code request; the old Worker on the new schema works.

items.title: Migration 0003 adds client_name/target_name and issueCode stores cleaned names

expected_outputs: every test file under tests/unit/services/account passes, including the new "device grant names (PAN-5071)" cases and the unchanged maintenance.test.ts

narrative.Action: Follow PRD W-1 exactly: create services/account/migrations/0003_device_grant_names.sql with two ALTER TABLE device_grants ADD COLUMN statements (client_name TEXT, target_name TEXT), no semicolons in comments; add client_name/target_name (string | null) to DeviceGrantRow; add exported DEVICE_NAME_MAX = 64 and deviceName() (strip \p{Cc} and bidi controls U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, trim, cut to 64 code points, trim, empty -> null); make issueCode INSERT the cleaned client_name and target_name form fields; update the device-flow.ts header comment; update schema.test.ts migration list and add the PRD W-1 tests.

items.title: Given an empty test D1, when applyMigrations runs, then schema.test.ts returns the list [0001_init.sql, 0002_account_page.sql, 0003_device_grant_names.sql] and a device_grants row inserted without the new columns reads client_name and target_name as null

When POST /oauth/device/code receives client_name "  grok-bot  " and target_name "eltmon-desktop", then the device_grants row stores "grok-bot" and "eltmon-desktop" and the JSON response contains exactly the six RFC 8628 fields
When client_name is 70 characters, then the stored value contains its first 64 characters; when client_name is whitespace-only and target_name is absent, then both columns store null
When client_name is "grok\u202Ebot\n", then deviceName returns and the row stores "grokbot"; deviceName(undefined) returns null and a 65-emoji input returns 64 code points
One confirmStep renderer names the bot and machine with an Authorize button for POST /activate

narrative.Action: Follow PRD W-2 exactly: add exported NAMES_ARE_CLAIMS_MESSAGE and a confirmStep(grant, normalized) function after activateForm that escapes every name, chooses the FR-27 lead sentence by which names are present (both, client only, target only, neither = today's sentence), adds the muted claims line only when a name is present, keeps the existing muted "Code XXXX-XXXX. If you did not start this sign-in, close this tab." line, and renders one button labelled Authorize posting the normalized code to /activate/confirm; replace the inline confirm page in activateSubmit with html(confirmStep(grant, normalizeUserCode(raw))); add the W-2 tests.

Given client-only, target-only and no-name grants, when POST /activate submits each code, then each page renders its FR-27 sentence and the no-name page still contains "Connect a Windows device" (win32) and does not contain NAMES_ARE_CLAIMS_MESSAGE
Given client_name "<script>alert(1)</script>" and target_name a"b, when the confirm step renders, then the body contains "<script>alert(1)</script>" and "a"b" and contains no "<script>"
When grep -rn "Continue with GitHub" services/account/src runs, then it returns no match, and approveInBrowser in device-flow.test.ts still produces a token on the next poll
GET /activate with a pending code renders the confirm step; wrong codes count against activate-fail

expected_outputs: device-flow.test.ts and routes.test.ts pass including the GET confirm, rate-limit, no-mutation and link-flow cases

narrative.Action: Follow PRD W-3 exactly: replace activatePage with the "After" handler (trim user_code; empty -> bare form 200 with no rate_limits access; else peek activate-fail and return rateLimitedPage when exhausted; a pending grant -> html(confirmStep(...)); otherwise hit activate-fail, 429 when the window fills, else the typed form prefilled with the formatted code and INVALID_CODE_MESSAGE at status 400); do not change routes.ts; replace the old GET prefill assertion at device-flow.test.ts lines 98-100 and add every W-3 test, including the full GET -> confirm -> callback -> token flow with no POST /activate.

items.title: Given a pending grant, when GET /activate?user_code=<lowercase undashed code> runs, then it returns 200 containing ">Authorize</button>", action="/activate/confirm" and the normalized hidden code, and the body does not contain autocomplete="off"
When GET /activate has no user_code or user_code=%20, then it renders the typed form with status 200 and SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rate_limits WHERE bucket = 'activate-fail' returns 0

When GET /activate?user_code=BBBB-BBBB (no grant) or an expired code runs, then it returns 400 containing INVALID_CODE_MESSAGE and records one activate-fail hit; the 11th wrong code from one IP (GETs and POSTs share the window) returns 429 with Retry-After, and a valid code from that IP then returns 429 while another IP returns 200
Given a pending grant, when GET /activate with its code runs, then SELECT * FROM device_grants returns a row equal to the row before the GET and the next poll returns authorization_pending

When the test follows the link (GET /activate?user_code, then POST /activate/confirm with the hidden code and same-origin Origin, then the GitHub callback), then the next poll returns an access_token with no POST /activate request made
Miniflare integration test opens the named activate link on real workerd and D1

items.title: When a reader opens docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md, then the device-flow paragraph contains client_name, target_name, the 64-character cut, "Authorize", and a sentence that a GET never changes a grant
